turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi! Nice to meet you too. Um, so I came in because I just feel like I absolutely cannot get my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time. It's a complete disaster. Like, my supplies, my due dates, receipts, assignment notes—they literally all just end up in these massive piles all over my room, and I just stare at them and I don't know what to do first. 

Which is a shame because the shop is actually doing pretty well! I make these little resin keychains and phone charms? I just got this huge shipment of these really cute star-shaped glass beads. I was trying to make these Y2K-style ones because they're selling super fast right now, especially the hot pink ones, but then my cat—his name is Barnaby, he's a total menace—he knocked over my entire tray of metal jump rings yesterday. It took me like an hour to pick them out of the rug, which is so annoying because the vacuum always eats them if I don't get every single one, and it makes this horrible rattling noise... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, yeah, just... everything is in piles and I can't keep track of anything.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly states they cannot get their schoolwork and shop organized, resulting in massive piles of supplies and notes and an inability to prioritize tasks.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility by unrelated thoughts, going off on a tangent about their cat and vacuum before losing their train of thought and asking, 'Wait, what was I saying?'

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized or high compared with your normal self?
turns.patient_response: Um, unusually energized or high? No, I don't think so. I mean, I always have a lot of energy, honestly. Like, my mom used to say I was like a wind-up toy that someone broke the knob off of when I was a kid. I was always running around, climbing on things. Actually, I still climb on things! Just last week I climbed up on top of my kitchen cabinets because I was trying to find this specific brand of instant ramen I bought like three months ago. It's this spicy seafood one? The packaging is bright orange, and it has this little cartoon octopus on it that looks so mad, it's hilarious. But anyway, I was up there, and I realized how dusty the tops of the cabinets were, so then I started cleaning them, but I didn't have any paper towels, so I used an old t-shirt... wait, no, I've never felt like, *unusually* high or energized. Just my normal amount, I guess.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes being easily distracted by extraneous stimuli, such as noticing dust while looking for ramen and abandoning the original task to start cleaning.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient admits to a history of running around and climbing on things, and notes they still climb on things, such as getting on top of kitchen cabinets.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes always having a lot of energy and being compared to a 'wind-up toy', which aligns with acting as if driven by a motor.
symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient explicitly denies ever having a distinct period of feeling unusually high or energized compared to their normal baseline.

turns.doctor_question: Did you have trouble paying attention or staying organized when you were a child?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, yeah, absolutely. Like, my mom actually still has a bunch of my old elementary school report cards and notes from teachers. They all basically say the same thing—that I was constantly out of my seat, or I'd just blurt out answers before the teacher even called on me. And whenever we had group activities, I would just rush through everything, even if I totally understood the assignment. I just couldn't wait. 

Speaking of my mom, she actually just texted me right before I came in here. She wanted to know if I wanted to go to this pottery painting place this weekend. Have you ever been to one of those? They're so fun. You just pick out a plain ceramic thing—last time I did a mug shaped like a frog, it's my favorite mug now, I drink all my matcha lattes out of it. Matcha is so much better than regular coffee, honestly. Coffee makes me feel too jittery, but matcha is like... a calm energy? Plus, the green color is just really aesthetically pleasing. I tried making my own matcha at home once, but I didn't have the little bamboo whisk thing, so I just used a fork, and it was so clumpy... 

But yeah, the school notes! Always out of my seat, always talking. That was me.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly agrees ('Oh, yeah, absolutely') to the doctor's question about having trouble paying attention as a child.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly agrees ('Oh, yeah, absolutely') to the doctor's question about having trouble staying organized as a child.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient notes that their elementary school report cards stated they were 'constantly out of my seat.'
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient confirms that their school notes described them as 'always talking.'
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient recalls that they would 'blurt out answers before the teacher even called on me.'
symptom_reasoning.S017: The patient describes rushing through group activities because they 'just couldn't wait.'

turns.doctor_question: Do these attention and organization problems happen in other parts of your life too, not just with school and your shop?
turns.patient_response:
Um, other parts of my life? I mean, I guess so? Like, I'm trying to think... it's just kind of everywhere, honestly. Like with my friends, I'm always the one who's late or forgets where we're supposed to meet. Oh! Speaking of my friends, my roommate Chloe and I were supposed to go to this vintage flea market last weekend. It's this huge one that happens once a month downtown, and people sell the coolest stuff. I was really hoping to find some vintage Levi's because the new ones just don't fit the same, you know? The denim is way too stretchy now. But anyway, we were supposed to go, and I totally lost my keys. Like, completely vanished. I spent forty-five minutes tearing my room apart, looking under my bed, in my laundry hamper—which, by the way, I really need to do laundry, I'm out of clean socks. I hate doing laundry, folding takes forever, so I usually just leave it in the basket and pick things out of it. 

But yeah, I finally found my keys inside the refrigerator next to a half-eaten container of hummus. I must have set them down when I was getting a snack? I love hummus, especially the roasted red pepper kind, but it goes bad so fast if you don't eat it right away. 

So yeah, I guess I do have trouble keeping things straight outside of school and the shop. It's just a lot to keep track of, you know?

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient mentions always being late and having trouble keeping things straight, indicating poor time management and organizational skills.
symptom_reasoning.S006: The patient avoids folding laundry because it 'takes forever,' showing reluctance to engage in tasks requiring sustained effort.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient describes losing their keys and spending 45 minutes looking for them before finding them in the refrigerator.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient's response is highly distractible, frequently derailing into unrelated thoughts about vintage jeans, laundry, and hummus.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient notes that they often forget where they are supposed to meet their friends for daily social activities.

turns.doctor_question: Have these attention and organization problems caused you to fail classes or lose jobs?
turns.patient_response:
Fail classes or lose jobs? Um, well, I guess not exactly fail classes, but it's definitely messing things up for me right now. Like, because of all this stuff, I missed some required steps for my program, and now my financial aid is totally at risk, which is stressing me out so much. Financial aid is literally the only way I can afford to go, and the forms are so complicated! They ask for all this tax stuff, and I'm just like, I'm 21, I barely know how to do my own taxes. I tried using one of those free online tax things last year, but I got stuck on this one question about deductions and just stared at the screen for like an hour. I ended up calling my dad, but he was watching a football game, so he wasn't really paying attention to me. He loves the Eagles, which is weird because we don't even live in Pennsylvania. He has this lucky jersey he wears every Sunday, it's so faded you can barely read the number anymore. 

But anyway, yeah, the financial aid thing is bad. And then with my shop projects, the people I work with have started depending on me less. Like, they don't give me the important parts to do anymore because they know I might forget or mess up the timeline. Which sucks, because I really like doing the hands-on stuff! I was supposed to paint this huge backdrop for our last project, and I had all these cool ideas for a sunset gradient, but they ended up giving it to Sarah instead. Sarah's nice, but she uses way too much purple, you know? Like, sunsets have pink and orange, not just dark purple. 

So yeah, it hasn't gotten me fired, but it's definitely causing some major problems.

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient mentions missing required steps for their program, indicating a failure to follow through on school-related duties.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient states that peers give them less responsibility on projects because they are known to forget things.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, wandering from the topic of financial aid to taxes, their father watching football, and his Eagles jersey.
